findings.title: Reflected XSS in Search Parameter
findings.evidence: The search parameter is reflected into the response without adequate output encoding.
findings.impact: An attacker may execute JavaScript in a victim's browser through a crafted search URL.
findings.remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and validate input before rendering it.

findings.title: Weak Authentication Configuration
findings.evidence: The authentication flow accepts weak password configuration in the synthetic test scenario.
findings.impact: Weak authentication controls can increase the risk of unauthorized account access.
findings.remediation: Apply stronger password requirements and appropriate authentication controls.

findings.title: Missing Security Header
findings.evidence: The HTTP response does not include the expected security header.
findings.impact: Missing browser security controls can increase exposure to certain client-side attacks.
findings.remediation: Configure the required security headers at the application or web-server layer.

findings.title: Exposed Debug Information
findings.evidence: The synthetic debug endpoint exposes implementation details in its response.
findings.impact: Exposed debug information can provide useful details to an attacker during reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Disable debug output in non-development environments and restrict diagnostic endpoints.

findings.title: Insecure CORS Configuration
findings.evidence: The synthetic API response allows an overly broad cross-origin policy.
findings.impact: A permissive cross-origin policy may allow unintended origins to access API responses.
findings.remediation: Restrict allowed origins to trusted domains and review credential handling.
